cards.title: 'Beta, yeh kaise karte hain?' Again.
cards.body: Teaching parents a new app tests everyone's patience. A few simple habits make it far less painful, for them and for you.

cards.title: 1. Start with one feature only
cards.body: Don't tour the whole app. Teach the single thing they'll use daily, like checking the next dose. Add more after a week.

cards.title: 2. Let them hold the phone
cards.body: Your fingers flying across their screen teaches nothing. Sit beside them and let them tap, even if it's slow.

cards.title: 3. Write the steps on paper
cards.body: Three numbered steps in big letters, kept near the phone. Screenshots with circles drawn on them work well too.

cards.title: 4. Make the text bigger first
cards.body: Increase the font and display size before you start. Half of 'I can't do this' is actually 'I can't read this'.

cards.title: 5. Expect repeat questions, stay kind
cards.body: Asking the same thing three times is normal with anything new. They taught you to hold a spoon. You can explain a button again.

cards.title: Patience is the real feature
cards.body: One feature, their hands, written steps, big text and kindness. That's how a health app actually gets used at home.

takeaway: Teach one feature at a time, let parents tap themselves, write the steps down, enlarge the text and stay patient.
share: Teaching Mummy Papa a new app? One feature, their hands, steps on paper, big text, patience.
